title: Pitch model answers at a strong student
statement: Pitch a model answer at what a strong student of the grade could write in the time, not at expert writing.
example: On the live proof, the judge's check that a model paragraph is something a strong Grade 9 student could write in about five minutes held with a confidence of 0.84 and 0.86.
detail: The writer prompts of four blocks in the lesson engine pitch their model writing at Grade 9 students, three of them at a strong one, and the claim-evidence-reasoning prompt at what such a student could write in five minutes. Two blocks also ask the judge, as an advisory check, whether the model could come from such a student: one asks whether a strong one could write it in about five minutes, the other whether both paragraphs read like Grade 9 writing rather than an adult critic's. On the live proof the first check held at p 0.84 and 0.86.
against: Both judge checks are advisory and never hold a block: the drama comparison's student-voice check came back unclear at p 0.59 and the block shipped. Nobody has measured whether students find the pitch right.
